Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
813 AM EDT Fri Oct 16 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
A Coastal Flood Advisory has been issued for Annapolis. See the
Tides/Coastal Flooding section below.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) A strong cold front brings gusty winds, potential for 
  severe weather, and below average temperatures.

- 2) Dry conditions through next week with temperatures 
  returning to mid-October normals.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...A strong cold front brings gusty winds, potential 
for severe weather, and below average temperatures.

Model guidance is in relatively good agreement showing a potent, 
positively-tilted trough stretching from the Great Lakes down 
towards the Great Plains tracking eastward this morning. At the 
surface, the trough pushes a strong cold front across the 
forecast area this afternoon and into the evening. This morning,
ahead of the front, cloud cover decreases allowing for sunny 
conditions and warm temperatures. Highs today rise into the 80s 
for most with higher elevations staying in the 70s. With warm 
conditions and sunny skies, a line of thunderstorms is expected 
to develop along the passing cold front. The Storm Prediction 
Center has much of the area east of the Blue Ridge/Catoctins and
north of US-50/I-66 in a Slight Risk (level 2 out of 5) for 
severe weather, driven primarily by a risk of damaging wind 
gusts. The highest probabilities are in the vicinity of NE MD 
(30% probs). Additionally, a quick QLCS tornado is possible, 
mainly in NE MD, where SPC also has a 2% tornado risk.

Precipitation lingers behind the cold front as the upper trough 
pivots overhead tonight. Gusty winds remain possible beginning 
this evening and persisting through Saturday. Winds will likely
remain elevated across most of the area, although the higher 
elevations along the Alleghenies may have the highest peak 
gusts (between 30 and 40 mph). All areas are expected to remain
below Wind Advisory criteria, although a few isolated gusts 
to near 45 mph are possible along the highest ridges.

Noticeably cooler temperatures rush in behind the front with 
high temperatures on Saturday being approximately 25-30 degrees 
colder compared to today. Highs on Saturday will be in the 40s 
and 50s across the forecast area with overnight lows dropping 
into the 30s to low 40s. Frost/Freeze headlines are likely for 
early Sunday morning, mainly west of I-95 where winds will be 
lower.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Dry conditions through next week with temperatures 
returning to mid-October normals.

Heading into next week, high pressure remains overhead through the 
middle of the week. A dry and benign weather pattern is expected
during this time with near normal temperatures for mid-October.
Although several global ensemble members depict a coastal low 
forming off the Mid-Atlantic shore early next week, most members
maintain dry and seasonable weather. If this low pressure 
system were to move closer to the coast, chances for 
precipitation could change next week, but confidence is low.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
MVFR to IFR ceilings continue through early this morning before
conditions improve quickly to VFR. Foggy conditions continue at
CHO this morning with patchy fog/mist lingering across the 
other terminals. A strong cold front crosses the terminals this 
afternoon and into this evening, bringing a chance for 
thunderstorms, gusty winds and a wind shift. Sub-VFR conditions 
are possible during storms. Some storms may be severe with 
damaging winds as the primary threat. Low clouds are possible 
again tonight with VFR conditions returning Saturday. For the 
winds, southwest winds this morning shift to northwest in the 
wake of the cold front. Winds remain out of the northwest on 
Saturday, gusting 20 to 30 knots. Winds diminish on Sunday with 
VFR conditions expected.

VFR conditions are expected to persist for all terminals at the 
beginning of next week. Light northeasterly wind on Monday shift 
northerly by Tuesday.

&&

.MARINE...
Small Craft Advisories are in effect across all waters with S
winds gusting 20 knots. A strong cold front crosses the waters 
this afternoon and into the evening, bringing gusty W/NW winds 
and a chance for thunderstorms. Special Marine Warnings are 
possible as storms cross the waters later today. Winds shift to 
northwesterly behind the front tonight and increase with gusts 
around 35 knots. The Gale Watch has been upgraded to a Gale 
Warning for late tonight through Saturday for the wider waters.
Winds shift to northeast on Sunday and are expected to remain 
below SCA criteria.

Wind gusts remain below SCA criteria on Monday with light 
northeasterly winds. Northerly winds could approach SCA criteria on 
Tuesday.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Southerly flow has resulted in rising water levels this morning,
with threshold minor flooding at Annapolis. Havre de Grace and
Alexandria could come close to minor, as well.

A cold front will shift winds to the west and northwest
resulting in decreasing water levels this evening. However, if
the front is even just an hour or two slower, these same 3 sites
could hit minor again this evening.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...

WV...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 6 AM EDT Saturday for ANZ530>543.
     Gale Warning from 6 AM Saturday to 6 AM EDT Sunday for 
     ANZ532>534-537-543.
